title: the dress that came back

opening.dialogue: At the win, the drivers sit with their engines off and their phones face-up: a life is a sending, and the soi mouth is where the sending is counted. Je Fah's shophouse back room glows behind a curtain, and the rack inside is labeled for tonight.

She holds the dress up to the rank's one streetlight and lets it hang there, a blue cotton with the temple-drive tag still pinned inside the hem. 'Nobody wore it. It came back to me washed. That's rotation, not theft.'
Bank leans on his bike, charger bank in one hand, and does not look at the dress. 'The bench watched it spin. The whole bench.'

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She drapes the dress over the laundry basket and presses the temple-drive tag flat with her thumb.
turns.dialogue: The donor's already waved it off — no problem, she said, it was for the flood. So it's no problem. I'm telling you it's no problem before anyone else tells me it is.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She tilts the ring light toward the dress and squints at the hem, then nods at Lek's face for confirmation.
turns.dialogue: This is the one, isn't it — the blue with the mended seam. I think that's right. I think it is. Say it's the one so I can stop looking at it.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She flaps one hand at the driver who has stepped up to ask about the dress, the other hand flat on the phone mount.
turns.dialogue: He's asking in the camp way and I'm answering in the market way and neither is landing. I can't speak that. You read for people — read this for me.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She lifts the lid of the biscuit tin with one finger, sniffs the old paper smell, and pushes it back across the counter toward Lek.
turns.dialogue: Your ledgers. Fine. I'll try it — I'll let the books say what the soi won't. Open it and show me what the dress cost the drive and what it costs the rack.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She wags one finger at the notebook in Lek's hand, then taps the ring light's switch without turning it on.
turns.dialogue: Write it down now, because I might change my mind by the time the live starts. I might change my mind twice. The light's warm and the room's cold and I'm both.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She steps out from behind the curtain with the phone mount still in her fist and sets it on the counter between them.
turns.dialogue: I heard everything. The bench, the driver, the donor's cousin — everything. So don't soften it for me now. Softening is a kind of standing still.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She scrolls the phone in the mount to last year's flood-drive photos and holds the screen up beside the dress.
turns.dialogue: Look at that. The whole soi in rubber boots, handing boxes. It was a good experience. It was. I want it to have been a good experience and not a stock intake.

turns.speaker: char_je_fah
stage_directions: She nods at the soi's one water buffalo grazing the last rai's edge, then at the dress, then at the stamp-drawer keys on Lek's belt.
turns.dialogue: That buffalo eats and eats and never stops to be thanked. The soi's like that with a story. It'll chew this dress all night unless someone stamps it done.

fah_turn_1.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_1.line: She pins the temple tag to the basket handle so it faces the rank, and the drivers read it without meaning to.

fah_turn_2.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_2.line: The ring light catches the mended seam and the whole rank sees the stitch was done by hand, not by a machine.

fah_turn_3.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_3.line: She sets the phone mount down and the driver steps back, waiting for a voice that can carry both ways.

fah_turn_4.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_4.line: The tin opens. Inside, three vendors' books and a folded receipt from the flood drive, dated last year, in Lek's own hand.
fah_turn_4.bubble: Lek's ledgers show the dress was logged as donated

fah_turn_5.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_5.line: She switches the ring light off. The back room goes dark and the dress is just cloth on a rack, waiting.

fah_turn_6.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_6.line: She turns the phone mount face-down on the counter. 'Then write it plain. The soi can read plain.'

fah_turn_7.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_7.line: The photo shows the donor handing over the same blue dress, smiling, and Je Fah's own hand reaching to take it.
fah_turn_7.bubble: The donor gave the dress to Je Fah's own hands

fah_turn_8.speaker: char_je_fah
fah_turn_8.line: She lifts the stamp-drawer keys off Lek's belt and weighs them. 'A stamp says it left the drive. A stamp says it arrived here. That's all a stamp says.'

finale.dialogue: She hangs the dress at the front of the rack, tag out, and turns the ring light on for the live. 'Tonight I sell a dress that came back. The soi can call it what it likes.'
The drivers' phones light up one by one as the live begins, and the soi mouth counts the sending the way it counts everything: by who arrives.

obj_biscuit_tin.name: the biscuit tin of ledgers
obj_biscuit_tin.description: Biscuit tin, lid bent from a decade of thumbs, three vendors' books inside and a folded flood-drive receipt in Lek's hand.

obj_word_notebook.name: the word notebook
obj_word_notebook.description: Pocket notebook, spine taped twice, words collected from other people's mouths and never paid for.

obj_stamp_keys.name: the stamp-drawer keys
obj_stamp_keys.description: Two brass keys on a wire ring, worn smooth, that open the copy shop's stamp drawer and nothing else.

obj_charger_bank.name: the charger bank
obj_charger_bank.description: Black power bank, corner chipped, one port loose, charged at the laundromat bench at midnight.

obj_ring_light.name: the ring light
obj_ring_light.description: Clip-on ring light, one LED dead, the light Je Fah sells by and the light the soi squints into.

obj_mattress_ad.name: the mattress ad printout
obj_mattress_ad.description: A4 printout of a mattress ad, corners curled, taped to the shophouse glass and peeling at one edge.

obj_share_envelope.name: the circle envelope
obj_share_envelope.description: Brown envelope with a share-circle payout inside, one member's name penciled and half-erased.

obj_laundry_basket.name: the laundry basket
obj_laundry_basket.description: Plastic basket, one handle cracked, a blue cotton dress draped over it with a temple-drive tag pinned to the hem.

obj_phone_mount.name: the phone mount
obj_phone_mount.description: Clamp mount for the live phone, rubber jaw worn shiny, angled at the rack and the curtain.

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She reads the flood-drive receipt upside down, correctly. 'So the drive logged it donated. And the rack logged it stock. Two books, one dress. Which book does the soi believe?'
outcomeRules.bubble: Je Fah has seen the flood-drive receipt

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She watches Lek write the donor's words in the notebook and stops him at the last line. 'Leave that one. If the soi reads it plain, it reads it plain. Don't polish my name.'
outcomeRules.bubble: The donor's words are written plain

outcomeRules.speaker: char_je_fah
outcomeRules.line: She takes the keys, opens the stamp drawer, and stamps the receipt 'returned to stock' — then stamps the dress tag 'sold, live, tonight.' 'Now both books say the same thing. The soi can audit a stamp.'
outcomeRules.bubble: The dress is stamped and the live can begin

char_je_fah: She turns the {item} over once and sets it back on the counter. 'Not that. The soi's already chewing this dress and I need something it can swallow.'
She taps the {item} against the laundry basket. 'The receipt's the thing. The drive logged it and the rack logged it and the two books don't agree.'
She holds the {item} up to the ring light. 'The flood-drive receipt first. Then the words. Then a stamp that says both books agree. In that order, or the soi writes its own order.'
narrator: The {item} goes back into the night with nothing settled. The drivers watch the curtain and the curtain stays closed.
Nothing comes of the {item} yet. Je Fah's thumb worries the temple tag on the dress hem, back and forth.
Je Fah's gaze flicks from the {item} to the biscuit tin to the stamp drawer and back — a route mapped, a toll implied.
